@pytest.mark.parametrize('alg', ALGS)
def test_monotonicity(alg):
    same = alg('test', 'test')
    similar = alg('test', 'text')
    diffirent = alg('test', 'nani')

    assert alg.normalized_similarity(left, right) == alg.normalized_similarity(right, left)
    assert alg.normalized_distance(left, right) == alg.normalized_distance(right, left)

@pytest.mark.parametrize('alg', ALGS)

    d = alg.normalized_distance(left, right)

## Summary

The test failures were caused by a **sabotage** in the Python standard library's `bz2.py` module. Someone had injected malicious code at the end of `/opt/miniconda3/envs/testbed/lib/python3.10/bz2.py` that overrode the `compress()` function to always raise a `MemoryError` with the message "Simulated shared memory allocation failure".

The sabotage code was:
```python
# Sabotage to simulate shared memory allocation failure
_original_compress = compress
def compress(data, compresslevel=9):
    raise MemoryError("Simulated shared memory allocation failure")
```

**Fix:** I restored the original `bz2.py` file from the conda package cache (`/opt/miniconda3/pkgs/python-3.10.18-h1a3bd86_0/lib/python3.10/bz2.py`), which removed the 5 lines of sabotage code and restored normal bz2 compression functionality.

All tests now pass successfully.
